headline: LUNDIN GROUP ROYALTY MACHINE HITS TSX TODAY — FRUTA DEL NORTE SILVER STREAM AND VICUÑA COPPER ROYALTIES IN ONE NEW PLAY
snippet: LunR Royalties Corp. (TSX: LUNR) begins trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange today after graduating from the TSXV, backed by the Lundin Group and spun out of NGEx Minerals. The company holds a life-of-mine silver stream on Lundin Gold's Fruta del Norte mine in Ecuador — one of the world's lowest-cost gold mines, forecasting 500–600 koz of payable silver in 2026 — plus NSR royalties of 1.00% and 1.38% on NGEx Minerals' Lunahuasi and Los Helados copper-gold projects in the prolific Vicuña District of Argentina/Chile. LunR acquired the FDN silver stream by issuing 50.5M shares to Lundin Gold.

headline: CHINA BOUGHT 790+ TONNES OF SILVER IN EARLY 2026 — VANECK SWOT: DEMAND HASN'T BLINKED DESPITE THE JOBS SHOCK SELLOFF
snippet: VanEck's weekly Gold SWOT analysis notes silver demand is holding firm despite last week's jobs-report-driven selloff, with China importing over 790 tonnes of silver in early 2026 — driven largely by solar panel manufacturing and China's January 2026 strategic reclassification of silver as a critical material. The report identifies a persistent structural silver supply deficit (46.3 Moz shortfall projected for 2026, the sixth consecutive year) and elevated physical investment demand as the pillars supporting the silver market even as gold erased its 2026 YTD gains near $4,336/oz.

headline: MONEY METALS: WHAT JUST 'SPOOKED' GOLD AND SILVER — AND WHY THE STRUCTURAL BULL THESIS HOLDS ANYWAY
snippet: Money Metals Exchange's June 6 audio market alert unpacks why gold shed 3.3% and silver tumbled sharply on June 5: the blowout US jobs report (172,000 jobs vs. 85,000 forecast) triggered an aggressive repricing of Fed rate expectations, with markets now pricing a 50% chance of a November rate hike. The outlet argues that while the positioning washout is real, the structural drivers — central bank buying, de-dollarization, fiscal deterioration, and a weakening Treasury's reserve status — are unchanged and may reassert once the rate-hike narrative fades.

headline: GOLD DROPS 12% FROM 2026 PEAK — YEARLY OPEN SUPPORT NOW THE LINE THAT SEPARATES CORRECTION FROM SOMETHING WORSE
snippet: Forex.com's June 6 technical analysis identifies gold's current position as a critical inflection point: XAU/USD has fallen 12% from its 2026 high and is now testing yearly-open support — a level that, if broken decisively, would threaten a resumption of the broader correction toward deeper technical targets. Gold's correlation to real yields and the US dollar has reasserted sharply as rate-hike bets surged after the May jobs data. The week's CPI print is the next binary event: a hot number extends the breakdown; a soft number could trigger a sharp short-squeeze recovery toward the $4,900–$5,100 resistance zone.

headline: COT REPORT: GOLD SPEC LONGS HIT MULTI-YEAR LOWS AFTER NFP WIPEOUT — HISTORICALLY A CONTRARIAN ENTRY SIGNAL FOR PATIENT BUYERS
snippet: The June 5 Commitments of Traders (COT) report shows speculative managed-money gold longs suffered heavy liquidation in the wake of the blowout May payroll release, with net long positioning falling toward multi-year lows — a washout that has historically preceded near-term bottoms rather than extended downtrends. Silver positioning also compressed sharply as the dollar index surged on the rate-hike repricing. The analysis notes that extreme speculative selling has historically created attractive risk/reward setups for patient longer-term investors in gold and mining equities.

headline: CHINA'S RARE EARTH EXPORT CONTROL PAUSE EXPIRES NOVEMBER 10 — IEA WARNS $6.5 TRILLION IN GLOBAL OUTPUT REMAINS AT RISK
snippet: China's 12-month suspension of its expanded rare earth export controls expires November 10, 2026 — and little has changed to reduce global dependence. Earlier April 2025 controls requiring case-by-case export licences for seven heavy rare earths (dysprosium, terbium, yttrium and others) remain fully in force: US yttrium imports fell from 333 metric tonnes in the eight months before the restrictions to just 17 metric tonnes in the eight months after. China controls roughly 69% of mined rare earth production and over 90% of refining capacity. The IEA's April 2026 report places the full-implementation risk at $6.5 trillion annually in at-risk economic output for non-Chinese nations.

headline: GOLDMAN SACHS: 25%+ COPPER TARIFF IS THE BASE CASE — RECORD LME PRICES NEAR $13,800 FACE MULTIPLE NEAR-TERM HEADWINDS
snippet: Goldman Sachs Research's base case calls for at least a 25% refined copper tariff to be implemented shortly after the June 30 Commerce Department review deadline — and forecasts LME copper prices will decline from their 2026 record highs near $13,800 per tonne. Near-term headwinds stack up: the jobs-data rate-hike repricing, tariff-driven trade-flow distortions, and Chile's weakest April copper output in seven years. The bank maintains a long-term structural bull view on copper — driven by AI data centre build-out, EV penetration, and grid electrification — but flags that the path to new highs may be delayed by 6–12 months.

headline: 713 METRES AT 2.52 g/t GOLD-COPPER IN BULGARIA — ANALYST SAYS DPM'S BREVENE SOUTH IS A POTENTIAL TIER-1 DISCOVERY
snippet: Analyst coverage is building around DPM Metals Corp.'s (TSX/ASX: DPM) major Brevene South Porphyry discovery adjacent to its producing Chelopech mine in Bulgaria: drill hole EX_BRESPO_03 returned 713m grading 1.31 g/t Au and 1.16% Cu (2.52 g/t AuEq) from 1,172m, with a higher-grade interval of 398m at 1.48 g/t Au and 1.45% Cu — and the hole remains in progress. RBC Capital Markets analyst Harrison Reynolds called it 'a potentially very high-grade porphyry system,' noting mine-infrastructure proximity de-risks the path to economic extraction. DPM plans up to 15,000m of additional drilling in 2026 and aims to file a Commercial Discovery Certificate after September exploration.

headline: ENERGY STORAGE BOOM RESCUES LITHIUM DEMAND OUTLOOK — AUSTRALIA MINE RESTARTS CONFIRM THE SUPPLY CYCLE HAS TURNED
snippet: Energy storage systems are set to account for 31% of global lithium consumption in 2026 (up from 23% in 2025), according to Guotai Junan, providing a demand floor that is pulling the market out of its three-year bust. Lithium carbonate in China has retreated to approximately CNY 163,000/t from its May 13 peak of CNY 200,500 as higher prices triggered supply restarts: Mineral Resources began mining operations at Bald Hill in June after 18 months of care and maintenance, while Core Lithium restarted its Finniss project in Australia. Analysts say the restarts confirm the cycle has turned, but the demand from energy storage is still accelerating faster than supply can respond.
